best_for: Office workers and anyone handling scanned paperwork who need to split, merge, rotate or reorder PDFs offline, without uploading private files to a website.

points.title: Six jobs, done offline
points.text: PDFsam Basic merges, splits, mixes, rotates, extracts and inserts pages. Everything runs on your computer, so files never go to a server and no internet connection is needed.

points.title: Splits that go beyond page numbers
points.text: You can split after given pages, every n pages, at bookmark levels or by rough file size. Merging can keep, drop or rebuild bookmarks and add a clickable table of contents.

points.title: Fixes single-sided scans
points.text: The Mix tool interleaves a file of odd pages with a file of even pages, with a reverse option for a flipped stack. That rebuilds a two-sided document from a one-sided scanner.

points.title: Free with no watermarks
points.text: Basic is open source under AGPL 3.0, free for company use, and adds no watermarks or size limits. You type page ranges rather than clicking thumbnails.

points.title: The paid editions are separate
points.text: PDFsam Visual (thumbnails, compression, cropping) is a 14-day trial, after which most of its tools need a license. PDFsam Enhanced is a Windows editor sold by yearly subscription. The Windows downloader offers Enhanced; the MSI listed here does not.

points.title: Light needs, 64-bit only
points.text: It needs a 64-bit system, about 256 MB of RAM and 70 MB of disk, with Java bundled. The download page lists Windows 10 or later and macOS 11 or later; 32-bit users are pointed to old version 3.3.7.

points.title: Easy to roll out
points.text: The Windows MSI installs for all users and supports silent install with properties. The Mac has separate Intel and Apple Silicon disk images. The Windows listing keeps 42 versions; macOS lists only the current release.
